title: Answer: no account of life, and the principles sought are substrate-independent

statements.text: Qualia formalism takes no position on what life is. The principles it seeks are meant to be substrate-independent, true of humans, other animals, aliens and conscious machines alike, and Principia Qualia doubts that a plausible formal theory of consciousness would leave the biological life of Earth holding most of the universe's qualia.
statements.scope: Principia Qualia (2016), the founding statement of the program

sources.locator: Clarifying the Problem of Valence, p. 6
sources.quote: universal, substrate-independent principles that apply equally to and are precisely true in all conscious entities
it would be surprisingly difficult to fully-formalize a plausible theory of consciousness where the biological life of Earth constitutes the majority of the universe's qualia
